# The manifests allowed to declare a package-manager lifecycle hook.
#
# `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` runs `preinstall`, `install`, `postinstall`, `prepare` and
# `prepublishOnly` from every manifest in the workspace — in every job, inside the composite
# action, before every verification in that job.
#
# Review finding [110]: the lane compared the declaration against a FIXED list of manifests, and
# `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is not that list. A pull request adding a package to the workspace with a
# `prepare` hook installed and ran it before any verification, and the lane never looked at that
# manifest because the declaration did not name it.
#
# So the refusal is here, in the pre-flight, BEFORE `pnpm install` runs: any `package.json` in
# the tree that declares one of those hooks must be on this list. Adding a package that needs
# one is a change to this file, in the diff, beside the package.
#
# One `<sha256>  <path>` entry per line, relative to the repository root.
#
# The digest is over the manifest's lifecycle PROJECTION — its hook keys and bodies, in a fixed
# order — and not over the whole file. Review finding [124]: being on this list permitted a
# manifest to run code at install time AND permitted that code to change unseen, so the root
# `preinstall` could quietly become a step that neuters every later guard shell in the job.
# Projecting rather than digesting the file keeps a dependency bump out of this diff and puts a
# change to what runs at install time squarely in it.
#
# Reseal with `node scripts/pin-guard-bytes.mjs`, which re-pins what the listed manifests run and
# never widens WHICH manifests are listed — that stays a human edit.
ea712b76d5dea7c495ffd2d5472f6b3894e749a0693f1ab145df7a4957c02070  package.json
3db2e6b28bf4117f860678d2f0e14c422319520751412635a7ed403797335ba0  packages/qfai/package.json
